title: Tottenham Press Conference LIVE: De Zerbi Addresses Pedro Porro Injury, Defeat & Ongoing Squad Issues
body:
Tottenham Hotspur’s manager Roberto De Zerbi faced a press conference fraught with frustration on Sunday, after his side fell 3‑2 to Aston Villa at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Saturday. The defeat not only extended the club’s winless run to three games but also saw promising right‑back Pedro Porro limp off the pitch with a serious injury just 15 minutes into the match, raising fresh concerns about squad depth and the team’s tactical cohesion.

De Zerbi opened by acknowledging the disappointment of the loss, noting that the team “started well enough to deserve a win” but failed to maintain concentration in the crucial phases of the game. He highlighted Villa’s resilience, especially after their equaliser in the 30th minute, and admitted that the Spurs’ defensive structure collapsed under pressure. “We gave away space in the middle and the full‑backs were caught out,” he said, pointing to the moments when Villa’s midfielders exploited the gaps left by a disorganised back line.

The injury to Porro, who had only joined the club in the summer, was a particular blow. The Spanish international was forced off after a hard challenge from Villa’s winger, sustaining what appeared to be a hamstring strain. De Zerbi expressed his concern for the player’s welfare, confirming that medical scans would be carried out within the next 24‑48 hours. “Pedro is a key part of our plan. He brings quality, pace and a different dimension to the right side. I hope it’s not serious, but we have to prepare for the worst,” he added. The uncertainty surrounding Porro’s fitness has forced De Zerbi to consider alternative options, potentially reshuffling the back four or turning to a more conservative three‑centre‑back system in upcoming fixtures.

Beyond the injury, the manager was candid about the broader issues that have plagued Spurs this season. He cited a lack of consistency in the attacking third, with Harry Kane and Son Heung‑min failing to convert clear chances, and a midfield that has struggled to dictate tempo against high‑pressing opponents. “We have talent, but we need to translate that into performance. The rhythm we showed against Villa in the first half evaporated because we lost the battle in the middle,” De Zerbi explained. He also addressed the criticism surrounding his tactical flexibility, conceding that the team has been “a bit rigid” and that he will look to introduce variations in formation and personnel to keep opponents guessing.

The manager’s comments also touched on the psychological aspect of the current slump. He admitted that the squad’s confidence has been dented after a string of narrow defeats, and that restoring belief will be as important as any tactical tweak. “We have to shake off the negativity and remember why we are here. The fans deserve a team that fights for every ball,” De Zerbi asserted, urging the supporters to remain patient while the club works through its injury list and tactical adjustments.

Looking ahead, De Zerbi outlined a roadmap for the next two weeks. Tottenham travel to face Brentford on Sunday, a match he described as a “must‑win” to halt the slide and regain momentum. He also hinted at possible rotation, with the possibility of giving younger players a chance to step up, especially if Porro’s recovery timeline extends beyond the immediate fixtures. The manager concluded by reaffirming his commitment to the club’s long‑term vision, emphasizing that “the foundation we are building will eventually bear fruit, but it requires resilience, hard work and a little patience from everyone involved.”

As Tottenham prepares for the Brentford clash, the twin challenges of shoring up a leaky defence and coping with a key player’s injury will test De Zerbi’s adaptability. Whether the Italian tactician can reverse the club’s fortunes before the winter break remains to be seen, but the next game will undoubtedly serve as a litmus test for both his strategic acumen and the squad’s resolve.
